analyst_view.overall: Hearts (32nd of 36, 1 point) host Monaco (4th, 9 points from 9) at a sold-out Tynecastle; Hearts have not won in Europe this season and need points, while Monaco are almost through. Wouter Vrancken's Hearts arrive after an 8-0 win at Dundee and are a settled side (about 84% of the eleven kept), but nine players including McEntee, Fagan-Walcott, Kingsley, Halkett and Spittal are out, all in the numbers (including a big cut for McEntee). Filipe Luís's Monaco miss Golovin, Ansu Fati and Idumbo (counted) plus young defender Elebi, who is not in the numbers but is not a regular starter; they rotate a fair amount (about 60% kept) with a Ligue 1 game on Sunday. Austrian referee Daniel Schlager, around average at 4.1 cards a game, is already counted. The match-day team-news page lists Idumbo, Golovin, Ansu Fati and Elebi out for Monaco and reports no new Hearts absences, so nothing new is big enough to move the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, 1.9 for Monaco, and already take big cuts for Hearts without McEntee and for Monaco without Brunner, Golovin and Idumbo. Monaco's usual rotation is part of their form and Hearts' big win at Dundee came against weak opposition, so I stay at 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners, nearly even, as Hearts tend to go direct and win set pieces at home while Monaco keep the ball. Nothing in the team news changes that, so I stay at 10.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards and already count referee Daniel Schlager, close to the average at 4.1 a game over 37 games. A loud Tynecastle and a Hearts side chasing the game could add a booking, but that is a hunch, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.9 shots and already trim Monaco for their lower recent shooting. Hearts are expected to keep a similar eleven and Monaco's rotation before Sunday's league game is normal for them, so I see no reason to move from 25.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target, 5.1 for Monaco. The absences that matter on both sides are already counted and Monaco's extra one, Elebi, is a fringe defender, so I stay at 8.8.
